cards.explanation: The answer is that many antichrists have appeared. The writer says they heard the antichrist is coming, and then he adds, "…now many antichrists have appeared." He doesn't say it's one lonely figure way off in the future. He says it's already happening, friends, and that's how he knows it's the last hour (1 John 2:18).

The answer is True. The writer says, "They went out from us, but they did not belong to us." So these antichrists were once around the believers, and then they left. That's the whole point of the verse, friends (1 John 2:19).

The answer is "remained." The writer says, "For if they had belonged to us, they would have remained with us." Staying is how he describes belonging here, friends. Their leaving made it clear that none of them belonged (1 John 2:19).

The answer is "all." The writer tells the believers, "You, however, have an anointing from the Holy One, and all of you know the truth." He doesn't pick out a smart few, bakers. That's good news for the whole batch (1 John 2:20).

The answer is False. The writer says he wrote to them "…because no lie comes from the truth." Truth doesn't produce lies, not even a little one, friends. He's also telling the believers they already have the truth (1 John 2:21).

The answer is whoever denies that Jesus is the Christ. The writer asks, "Who is the liar, if it is not the one who denies that Jesus is the Christ?" Then he says this is the antichrist, who denies the Father and the Son. He answers his own question right there in the verse, bakers (1 John 2:22).

The answer is False. The writer says, "Whoever denies the Son does not have the Father, but whoever confesses the Son has the Father as well." So the one who denies the Son does not have the Father, friends. The one who confesses the Son has the Father as well (1 John 2:23).

The answer is True. The writer says, "As for you, let what you have heard from the beginning remain in you." That's their job, friends, and he follows it with a promise. If it remains, they'll remain in the Son and in the Father (1 John 2:24).

The answer is eternal life. The writer says, "And this is the promise that He Himself made to us: eternal life." It's a promise that comes from Him, and the writer counts himself in with the believers when he says "to us." That's worth saying LOUD, friends: ETERNAL LIFE (1 John 2:25)!

The answer is those who are trying to deceive them. The writer says, "I have written these things to you about those who are trying to deceive you." So everything about the antichrists and the lies was written with those deceivers in mind, bakers. He's looking out for the believers (1 John 2:26).

The answer is to remain in Him as they were taught. The writer says, "…so remain in Him as you have been taught." The anointing teaches them about all things, and he tells them to stay in Him, friends. That's the same word he used for the message staying in them (1 John 2:27).
